response.title: FY2027 Budget Request: Opening a Sixth Harborlight Site
response.dek: Staff want the board to approve a $1,610,000 budget for FY2027 so Harborlight can open a sixth site at the Eastgate branch library and cut down a growing waitlist.

stat.label: Adults still on the waitlist when FY2026 ended

sections.heading: The staff request
sections.body: Staff recommend a budget of $1,610,000 for FY2027. The money would open a sixth site at the Eastgate branch library and pay for two more site coordinators. Staff think the new site would serve 180 more learners each year. They also expect it to cut the waitlist in half.

sections.heading: A growing need
sections.body: Harborlight enrolled 1,148 adult learners in FY2026, up from 936 the year before. Still, 287 adults were waiting for a spot at year end. Most were waiting at the Eastgate and Riverside sites. On average, they waited nine weeks.

sections.heading: FY2026 results
sections.body: Sixty-eight percent of learners who stayed at least 12 weeks moved up one or more reading levels. Seventy-one learners earned a high school equivalency credential, more than in any year before. Harborlight's 214 volunteer tutors gave 9,870 hours of tutoring.

sections.heading: Spending and reserves
sections.body: Harborlight spent $1,420,000 to operate in FY2026, and 81 percent of that went to programs. Foundation grants brought in $640,000, individual donors $388,000, and the city contract $295,000. Each learner cost $1,237. Reserves cover 3.2 months of operating costs, which is short of the board's 4-month goal.

points.text: Staff estimate the new site would serve 180 more learners each year
Adults waited nine weeks on average for a spot
Harborlight has 11 full-time staff, four of them site coordinators
Reserves cover 3.2 months, below the 4-month goal

quote.text: I read my granddaughter a bedtime story for the first time this spring.
quote.who: A learner at the Riverside site

response.next: The board agreed to vote on the FY2027 budget at its meeting on October 21.
